entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū al-Ḥasan Alī ibn al-Abbās ibn Jūrayj, also known as Ibn al-Rūmī, was a prominent Arab poet of Baghdād in the Abbāsid-era, tracing his lineage back to George the Greek, a historical figure of significant cultural influence.

  Born in the 9th century, Ibn al-Rūmī's literary works, primarily in the genre of qasida, have left a lasting impact on Arabic poetry, with many of his poems still studied and admired today for their mastery of language and theme.

  As a key figure in the intellectual and artistic movements of Baghdad during this period, Ibn al-Rūmī's works not only reflected the cultural exchange and syncretism of the time but also contributed to shaping the poetic traditions of the Islamic Golden Age.

  His poetry, characterized by its depth, nuance, and emotional resonance, continues to captivate readers and scholars alike, offering a unique window into the spiritual, social, and political dynamics of this pivotal era in Islamic history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ibn al-Rūmī's poetry played a significant role in shaping the poetic traditions of the Islamic Golden Age and preserving Arabic literature. His works, primarily in the genre of qasida, contributed to the development of Arabic poetry and its enduring popularity.
